name: Orlah (Forbidden Fruit of First Three Years — Laws)
notes: Detailed laws of orlah: what trees are subject, counting years, replanting, uprooting, grafting, and geographical differences (Israel, Syria, outside Israel)

name: Orlah Exemption Based on Purpose of Planting
notes: A tree planted as a fence or for lumber is exempt from orlah; if planted partly for food and partly for fence, the food-facing part is subject

name: Replanted Tree and Orlah Counting
notes: Rules for whether a uprooted and replanted tree restarts the orlah count, depending on whether it could survive on its own root

name: Bent-Down Shoot (Hiluch) and Orlah
notes: Laws of a layered/bent-down shoot: whether it takes on the status of its parent tree or is counted anew for orlah

name: Orlah in Syria and Outside the Land
notes: Geographical distinctions in orlah law: doubtful orlah is forbidden in Israel, permitted in Syria, and outside Israel one may purchase but not personally gather

name: Bitul b'Matayim (Nullification in Two Hundred and One)
notes: Orlah and kilayim of the vineyard are nullified in a mixture of 201 parts, unlike terumah which is 101; detailed rules for this ratio

name: Nullification of Kilayim of the Vineyard (Bitul)
notes: Rules for how kilayim of the vineyard become nullified in mixtures, how it combines with orlah, and when it can void terumah

name: Flavor Imparted by Forbidden Substance (Noten Ta'am)
notes: When a forbidden substance imparts flavor to a mixture it prohibits the whole; distinction between same-species (follows flavor imparting) and different species (follows nullification ratio)

name: Leaven That Causes Fermentation in Mixtures
notes: Rules for when orlah or kilayim leaven ferments dough: prohibition depends on whether there is sufficient leaven to ferment; cases where hullin and terumah leaven combine

name: Seasoning That Flavors a Dish (Me'abeid/Metzamtzem)
notes: When forbidden seasonings (orlah, terumah, kilayim) season a dish, the dish may be prohibited; rules differ by species type and by whether there is sufficient amount to season

name: Items Sold by Count That Cannot Be Nullified
notes: Certain items sold individually (e.g., soft-shelled nuts, pomegranates, loaves) are not nullified even in 201; Rabbi Meir vs. Sages dispute; list of six (or seven) such items

name: Asherah Tree — Prohibition of Use
notes: Leaves, sprouts, and sap from an Asherah (idolatrous tree) are forbidden for benefit; contrasted with orlah in what they prohibit

name: Garment Dyed with Orlah — Burning Requirement
notes: A garment dyed with orlah peels must be burned; if mixed with other garments, Rabbi Meir requires all to be burned while Sages nullify in 201

name: Oven Heated with Orlah Wood — Bread Baked in It
notes: Bread baked in an oven heated with orlah shells must be burned; if mixed with other loaves, it is nullified in 201

name: Fourth-Year Vineyard Produce Laws (Kerem Revay/Neta Revay)
notes: Fourth-year fruit is subject to different rules from orlah: certain items (leaves, sprouts) are permitted in regard to the fourth year though restricted under orlah

name: Doubtful Status in Chadash, Orlah, and Kilayim — Geographical Distinctions
hebrew: סָפֵק עָרְלָה, כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, חָדָשׁ — בְּמָקוֹמוֹת שׁוֹנִים
notes: The last mishnah in Orlah distinguishes the rabbinic vs. Torah status and handling of doubtful orlah, kilayim, and chadash in Israel, Syria, and abroad
